metaDescription: Connect Slack to Zapier to send automated channel messages, direct notifications, and status updates from your other apps.
intro: When something important happens in another app, your team often finds out too late because no one checked the dashboard. This guide shows how to connect Slack to Zapier, choosing between sending channel messages, direct messages, or status updates, and formatting them with rich text and dynamic data so alerts land where your team is already working.

steps.heading: Create a new Zap
steps.body: Open the Zapier dashboard and start a new workflow.

steps.heading: Select Slack from the app directory
steps.body: Choose Slack and review the available trigger or action events.

steps.heading: Authenticate your Slack account
steps.body: Sign in and approve the required workspace access permissions and scopes.

steps.heading: Choose your channel or recipient
steps.body: Select the target Slack channel or direct message recipient for your notifications.

steps.heading: Craft your message template
steps.body: Write your message text and map dynamic data tokens from previous app triggers directly into it.

steps.heading: Customize bot branding and test
steps.body: Set a custom bot name and profile icon, then run an end-to-end test to verify live alert delivery.

faq.question: Can I send a Slack message from any app event?
faq.answer: Yes, you can map dynamic data tokens from any trigger app into your Slack message template.

faq.question: Can I customize how the bot appears in Slack?
faq.answer: Yes, you can set a custom bot name and profile icon to match your branding.

faq.question: Can messages go to a specific person instead of a channel?
faq.answer: Yes, you can choose Send Direct Message as the action instead of posting to a channel.

faq.question: What permissions does Zapier need in my Slack workspace?
faq.answer: You'll need to authenticate your Slack account and approve the required workspace access permissions and scopes during setup.
